overview: Al-Kamil was Ayyubid sultan of Egypt during the Fifth Crusade and the ruler who negotiated Jerusalem’s temporary return to Frederick II in 1229.
His legacy is one of pragmatic rule: he could fight crusaders fiercely and also negotiate Jerusalem when political circumstances made treaty preferable.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Al-Kamil was Ayyubid sultan of Egypt during the Fifth Crusade and the ruler who negotiated Jerusalem’s temporary return to Frederick II in 1229.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Al-Kamil was a son of Al-Adil I and inherited a political world shaped by Ayyubid family partitions and crusader pressure on Egypt.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Al-Kamil, the Ayyubid sultan of Egypt, is remembered for an extraordinary act of diplomacy that defied the logic of holy war: his negotiated surrender of Jerusalem to the excommunicated emperor Frederick II in 1229, achieved without a battle. The sources, Muslim and Christian alike, present a pragmatic and intelligent ruler who preferred negotiation to bloodshed and who startled both sides by treating with the crusader emperor as a fellow sovereign and near-equal in curiosity.

His willingness to bargain away Jerusalem drew criticism in the Muslim world, but it reflected a calculating mind that valued Egypt's security over symbolic possession of the holy city. He is also remembered for his celebrated meeting with Francis of Assisi during the Fifth Crusade, an encounter that tradition presents as marked by courtesy and mutual respect.

What the record supports is a sophisticated, flexible, and intellectually curious ruler, more interested in practical advantage and cultural exchange than in ideological rigidity. He is remembered as the sultan who gave up Jerusalem by treaty — a pragmatic and worldly statesman whose diplomacy with Frederick II remains one of the most surprising episodes of the crusading age.

contentSections.title: As sultan of Egypt
paragraphs: During the Fifth Crusade, al-Kamil defended Egypt against the crusader occupation of Damietta. Later, facing Ayyubid rivalries and Frederick II’s diplomacy, he negotiated the Treaty of Jaffa in 1229.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Al-Kamil died in 1238 after a reign marked by diplomacy, war, and contested Ayyubid family politics.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: His legacy is one of pragmatic rule: he could fight crusaders fiercely and also negotiate Jerusalem when political circumstances made treaty preferable.
